:::{#exm-fisher-scoring-poisson}
#### Fisher scoring for Poisson data

For $\dsn{X} \siid \Pois(\rate)$,
the score is $\score(\rate) = n\bar x/\rate - n$
and the expected information is $\einf(\rate) = n/\rate$
(@exm-information-poisson), so one Fisher scoring step from any $\esttmpl > 0$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\esttmpl + \inv{\einf(\esttmpl)} \score(\esttmpl)
&= \esttmpl + \frac{\esttmpl}{n}\paren{\frac{n\bar x}{\esttmpl} - n}
&& \text{(substitute $\einf$ and $\score$)}\\
&= \esttmpl + \bar x - \esttmpl
&& \text{(distribute $\esttmpl/n$)}\\
&= \bar x
&& \text{(cancel $\esttmpl$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So Fisher scoring reaches the MLE $\bar x$ in one step,
while Newton-Raphson needs several (@tbl-mle-converge).
:::
